speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that background. To narrow this down, have you noticed any fever or chills accompanying the right flank pain and hematuria?

speaker: Patient
text: 42-year-old Caucasian male. The patient reports experiencing visible blood in his urine accompanied by discomfort in his right flank. He denies any recent trauma to the area. He mentions a series of urinary tract infections over the past few years but has not been on renal dialysis.

speaker: Doctor
text: Have you noticed any flank pain radiating to your groin, or have you experienced any nausea, vomiting, or fever since the onset of symptoms?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Hematuria and right flank pain. I also have History of recurrent urinary tract infections, No recent trauma.

speaker: Doctor
text:
REQUEST TEST: Urinalysis with microscopy and urine culture.
REQUEST TEST: Renal ultrasound.
Have you noticed any passing of small, sand-like particles or severe colicky pain that comes and goes?

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Urinalysis shows Appearance: Reddish, WBC: 10-20 /HPF, RBC: Too numerous to count, Nitrites: Negative, Leukocyte_Esterase: Positive. Renal Ultrasound (Intravenous Pyelogram) findings: Multiple cysts present in the collecting ducts of the medulla. No obstruction noted.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Medullary Sponge Kidney.

The presence of multiple cysts in the collecting ducts combined with your history of recurrent infections and "sand-like" particles suggests this congenital anomaly, where dilated tubules predispose you to stone formation and infection. Do you currently experience any passing of kidney stones or severe colicky pain?
